summary: Offboarded contractor left active GSuite service accounts, SSH keys on multi-region loaner devices, and lingering KMS access - runbook clarification
description:
Issue summary: Contractor CT-448 (term ended 2026-03-02) was deprovisioned via HR + Okta, but multiple residual credentials and hardware bindings were discovered after exit verification. Impact: potential unauthorized access surface due to active GSuite service account keys, SSH host keys present on loaner laptops in EU and US, and a service account still authorized on a KMS key policy. We need clarity on runbook steps to ensure complete credential sweep and a short remediation plan to remove/stage long-lived credentials.

Context: HR submitted standard offboarding on 2026-03-02 and tagged security and IT. Okta deprovision indicated SCIM user disabled. Contractor returned a loaner laptop to the UK office and an external hard drive to the SF office. During a routine audit on 2026-03-08, SRE noticed: (1) active GSuite service account JSON key used by a personal CI job, (2) SSH keys still listed in jump-host authorized_keys referencing contractor username, (3) KMS IAM policy includes a binding for service-account-ct448@redwood-internal. The audit also flagged a duplicate directory record which suggests SCIM may have created a disabled-but-not-deleted stub.

Requested outcome: Confirm immediate remediation steps taken, finalize a checklist for multi-region hardware returns, and update offboarding runbook to cover long-lived service credentials and KMS bindings.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run internal inventory script inventory/loans --owner ct-448 to list devices assigned
2) Query Okta SCIM logs for user provisioning events for ct-448 between 2026-02-25 and 2026-03-05
3) Check Google Cloud IAM audit logs for keys created by service-account-ct448@redwood-internal and last access times
4) Inspect jump-hosts (ssh-jump-us, ssh-jump-eu) authorized_keys for lines containing ct-448 or ct-448@personal-email
5) Check KMS key IAM bindings for any principal containing ct448 or service-account-ct448
6) Confirm GitHub deploy keys and repo-level collaborators for repos tagged with ct-448-project
Expected: all artifacts removed or rotated during offboarding; Actual: multiple artifacts remain active.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-09 09:12 - Maya: Initial report after daily credential audit flagged anomalies. Attached quick list of artifacts found.

2026-03-09 11:05 - Arjun: Checked Okta - user was set to "DEPROVISIONED" via SCIM but a secondary duplicate account (scim_stub_ct448) exists and is disabled-only in Okta - not deleted. SCIM outbound logs show a 409 conflict at 2026-03-02:12:04:11 when attempted deletion from HR system; likely allowed a disabled stub to remain.

2026-03-09 13:30 - EngOps: Found active GSuite service-account JSON key last-used 2026-03-07 by a personal CI runner (runner-personal-34) which is not on the approved runners list. Key rotation has not been enforced by automation for service accounts created before 2025-10.

2026-03-09 15:00 - Infra: Jump-hosts still reference ct-448 in authorized_keys on both ssh-jump-us (last modified 2026-03-04) and ssh-jump-eu (last modified 2026-03-05). No ticket existed to remove those entries post-return.

2026-03-10 08:47 - Security: KMS IAM policy for projects/prod-data/keys/analytics-key shows role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter bound to service-account-ct448@redwood-internal with date added 2025-11-20. No conditional or expiry was set.

Hypothesis: The offboarding runbook failed to handle older pre-2025 long-lived service-account keys, and SCIM errors created a disabled stub that skipped downstream hooks which clean service account bindings and queued removal of SSH keys.
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-09 09:18): Adding initial artifact list. See internal audit CSV: /confluence/display/OPS/credential-audit-2026-03-08
Arjun Patel (2026-03-09 11:20): I'll take ownership of immediate cleanup for GSuite keys and jump-host entries. Planning to rotate KMS bindings with Security's help. Pinging @security-team.

Lena Ortiz - Security (2026-03-09 12:10): Recommend disabling the service account first, then delete keys and rotate any secrets. For KMS, we should add a temporary deny binding for the principal while we assess. Will open a quick PR to policy repo.

SRE Lead - Tomas Novak (2026-03-10 09:05): We should also add a job to the nightly inventory to flag service accounts with human-owned emails and keys older than 90 days. Filing follow-up automation task INT-990322.

Arjun Patel (2026-03-11 14:33): Clean-up actions executed: (a) disabled service-account-ct448 in GCP, (b) revoked all active JSON keys (audit attached), (c) removed ct-448 lines from both jump-host authorized_keys, (d) rotated GitHub repo deploy keys referencing ct-448, (e) submitted PR #1427 in infra-as-code to add temporary deny binding for KMS key. Awaiting KMS policy approval and KMS key rotation window.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 10:02 - Short-term remediation completed: service account disabled and JSON keys revoked; jump-host entries removed; GitHub deploy keys rotated.
KMS action pending: Security requested scheduled rotation window for projects/prod-data/keys/analytics-key. Target rotation: 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC. Action owner Security (Lena Ortiz).
Workaround: Added temporary deny binding to KMS policy to prevent service-account-ct448 from decrypting until rotation completes. This is documented in infra PR #1427.
Post-mortem action items: runbook update, SCIM conflict handling, nightly inventory rule, and automation ticket INT-990322 for nightly scanning and automated credential-revocation triggers.
Follow-up: Schedule a 30-minute runbook sync with HR, IT Ops, and Security to finalize multi-region hardware returns and long-lived credential handling. Proposed time: 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC.
